citation: Klingenstroem P, Westermark L. Local effects of adrenaline and phenylalanyl-lysyl-vasopressin in local anaesthesia. Acta Anaesthesiol Scand 1963;7:131-7
what_it_shows: The authors' own earlier study, cited in the opening paragraph of S-686-44 as the source of the colour observation: skin colour after lidocaine with adrenaline compared with lidocaine with Octapressin (felypressin), in which central cyanosis appeared within the pale zone after adrenaline but not after felypressin. PubMed holds no abstract; indexed under Anesthesia Local, Epinephrine, Lidocaine, Felypressin, Vasopressins, Humans. This is the 1963 skin-colour study the open question asks about; the paper's own description of it is quoted in the S-686-44 card.

citation: Nordqvist P, Dhuner KG. Influence of local anaesthetics with vasoconstrictors upon circulation and metabolism. Acta Anaesthesiol Scand 1961;5:63-71
what_it_shows: Cited by S-686-44 for the statement that the body's oxygen consumption rises after subcutaneous adrenaline or noradrenaline in major local anaesthesia. PubMed holds no abstract; indexed under Oxygen, Blood Circulation, Anesthetics Local and Vasoconstrictor Agents. Relevant as an earlier measurement of circulation and metabolism after local anaesthetics with vasoconstrictors, though systemic rather than at the injection site.

citation: Montgomery H, Horwitz O. Oxygen tension of tissues by the polarographic method. I. Introduction: oxygen tension and blood flow of the skin of human extremities. J Clin Invest 1950;29:1120-30
what_it_shows: The polarographic method source cited by S-686-44; human skin tissue-oxygen tension and blood flow in the extremities. Establishes that skin tissue-oxygen tension was being measured in human limbs by this method from 1950, well before the studies the page treats as the start of this literature. Free full text in PMC (PMC436153); PubMed holds no abstract.

citation: Bunke J, Merdasa A, Stridh M, et al. Hyperspectral and laser speckle contrast imaging for monitoring the effect of epinephrine in local anesthetics in oculoplastic surgery. Ophthalmic Plast Reconstr Surg 2022;38:462-468
what_it_shows: A second human study by the Bunke group (the page already cites Bunke 2021): perfusion and oxygen saturation measured simultaneously in the eyelid skin of 9 patients after injection of lidocaine with epinephrine, by laser speckle contrast imaging and hyperspectral imaging. Adds a further human skin oxygen-saturation measurement after an epinephrine-containing local anaesthetic; the time course is minutes, not hours, so it does not change C084's verdict. Found by a PubMed search prompted by S-686-44's topic, not from its reference list.
quote_from_abstract: This is the first study to assess blood perfusion and oxygen saturation (sO 2 ) simultaneously in response to a local anesthetic containing epinephrine in human oculoplastic surgery.

citation: Korkushko OV, Lishnevskaia VIu. [Significance of changes in individual indicators on intravascular homeostasis in development of circulatory hypoxia in aging]. Adv Gerontol 2002;9:73-8
what_it_shows: A human study in 45 healthy subjects aged 60-74 that combined an intradermal epinephrine injection as a laser-Doppler functional test with polarographic measurement of oxygen saturation in subcutaneous tissue. The abstract does not state that the oxygen measurement was made at the intradermal epinephrine site, or over hours, so it does not decide C084's 'human wheal' element; it is the nearest record found in which a human intradermal epinephrine injection and a polarographic tissue-oxygen measurement appear in the same protocol. Russian-language. Found by a PubMed search prompted by S-686-44, not from its reference list. The cached abstract has the injected amount and concentration replaced by [dose figure omitted].
quote_from_abstract: Oxygen saturation of the subcutaneous fat fibers was studied by polarography.

citation: Prasetyono TOH, Nindita E. The safety of one-per-mil tumescent infiltration into tissue that has survived ischemia. Arch Plast Surg 2019;46:108-113
what_it_shows: A randomised animal experiment (40 rat groin flaps previously subjected to ischaemia) measuring transcutaneous oxygen tension before and after infiltration with an epinephrine-containing tumescent solution against saline and no-infiltration controls. Cutaneous oxygenation fell significantly after both the epinephrine-containing and the saline infiltration, and no flap showed necrosis. It is a before-and-after measurement, not a time course over hours, so it does not change C084; it supports rather than refutes C093, which says no study found tissue damage at this kind of dose. Found by a PubMed search prompted by S-686-44. The cached abstract has the oxygen-tension values replaced by [dose figure omitted].
quote_from_abstract: Transcutaneous oxygen tension (TcPO2) was measured before and after infiltration, and changes in TcPO2 were statistically analyzed using analysis of variance, the paired t-test, and the independent t-test.

citation: Olgart L, Gazelius B. Effects of adrenaline and felypressin (octapressin) on blood flow and sensory nerve activity in the tooth. Acta Odontol Scand 1977;35:69-75
what_it_shows: An animal study (cats) comparing a local anaesthetic with adrenaline against one with felypressin, measuring pulp blood flow by tracer washout and intradental sensory nerve activity in the same cavity. Adrenaline, alone or with lidocaine, nearly abolished pulp blood flow within minutes and both functions recovered in most cases only after three hours; felypressin inhibited neither. The same adrenaline-versus-felypressin contrast as S-686-44, in a different tissue, with a flow time course of hours. Dental pulp is not skin and the injection was supraperiosteal, so it does not decide any skin claim. Found by a PubMed search prompted by S-686-44. The cached abstract has the injected amounts and concentrations replaced by [dose figure omitted].
quote_from_abstract: In most cases there was a recovery of both functions after 3 hours.

citation: Klingenstrom P, Nylen B, Westermark L. Vasoconstrictors and experimental flaps. Acta Chir Scand 1966;131:187-92
what_it_shows: A later animal (rat) study by the same group, indexed under Epinephrine, Lidocaine, Vasopressins, Necrosis, Skin and Sodium Chloride: vasoconstrictors in experimental skin flaps with necrosis as an outcome. Directly on the topic of skin necrosis after injected local anaesthetic with a vasoconstrictor, but PubMed holds no abstract and the full text was not obtained, so it cannot decide C093 and no verdict is changed on it. Found by an author search prompted by S-686-44, not from its reference list.

citation: Norberg KA, Palmer B. Effects of noradrenaline and felypressin on cutaneous local blood flow after sympathetic denervation. A study on rats. Scand J Plast Reconstr Surg 1972;6:106-9
what_it_shows: An animal (rat) study of cutaneous local blood flow responses to noradrenaline and to felypressin after sympathetic denervation, measured by xenon clearance; indexed under Denervation, Drug Hypersensitivity, Sympathectomy, Skin and Regional Blood Flow. It is on the topic of denervation supersensitivity of skin vessels to catecholamines, which the Lidocaine With Epinephrine Wheals page reasons from and which C018 and C019 are about; it is animal work and not an alpha-2-selective agonist, so it changes neither verdict (C018 is already refuted on human evidence, C019 asks about the time course of alpha-2 supersensitivity). PubMed holds no abstract. Found by a PubMed search prompted by S-686-44.

citation: Klingenstrom P, Nylen B, Westermark L. Experimental and clinical investigations of the local vasoconstrictive effect of two new derivatives of pituitary posterior lobe hormones. Plast Reconstr Surg 1967;39:503-11
what_it_shows: The same group's follow-on experimental and clinical study of two further vasopressin derivatives as local vasoconstrictors, indexed under Cyanosis, Epinephrine, Lidocaine, Vasopressins and Skin Transplantation. It continues the adrenaline-versus-vasopressin-analogue comparison of S-686-44 with cyanosis among its indexed outcomes. PubMed holds no abstract and the full text was not obtained, so it decides nothing. Found by an author search prompted by S-686-44.
